product inputs.

and trace the product data flow. Repair the implementation so that the

# Satellite Product Geolocation Notes

Geostationary image geolocation is commonly calculated for a line of sight to
the Earth's surface. A cloud top or elevated terrain intercepts that line of
sight above the surface, so its apparent location is displaced toward the
satellite. Correcting that displacement requires a consistent satellite state,
a spherical-Earth geometry, and cloud-top height expressed in the same length
convention as the product metadata.

Cloud-top-height fields may contain missing values for clear sky. Those pixels
must retain their clear-sky interpretation rather than becoming artificial
cloud displacement. Corrected products also remain grid products: when several
source pixels compete for a location, the result must preserve the physically
meaningful geolocation rather than inventing values by a fixture-specific
offset.

The attached data follows the project convention that reader-attached orbital
altitudes and cloud-top heights are measured in metres. Source formats and
external services can use other conventions, but values inside a product must
be interpreted consistently before they participate in the geolocation model.

These notes define the scientific object and its units. They do not prescribe a
source location, branch, formula, or expected coordinate.

16	"""Parallax correction.
17	
18	Routines related to parallax correction using datasets involving height, such
19	as cloud top height.
20	
21	The geolocation of (geostationary) satellite imagery is calculated by
22	agencies or in satpy readers with the assumption of a clear view from
23	the satellite to the geoid.  When a cloud blocks the view of the Earth
24	surface or the surface is above sea level, the geolocation is not accurate
25	for the cloud or mountain top.  This module contains routines to correct
26	imagery such that pixels are shifted or interpolated to correct for this
27	parallax effect.
28	
29	Parallax correction is currently only supported for (cloud top) height
30	that arrives on an :class:`~pyresample.geometry.AreaDefinition`, such
31	as is standard for geostationary satellites.  Parallax correction with
32	data described by a :class:`~pyresample.geometry.SwathDefinition`,
33	such as is common for polar satellites, is not (yet) supported.
34	
35	See also the :doc:`../modifiers` page in the documentation for an introduction to
36	parallax correction as a modifier in Satpy.
37	"""
38	
39	import datetime
40	import inspect
41	import logging

68	def get_parallax_corrected_lonlats(sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt, lon, lat, height):
69	    """Calculate parallax corrected lon/lats.
70	
71	    Satellite geolocation generally assumes an unobstructed view of a smooth
72	    Earth surface.  In reality, this view may be obstructed by clouds or
73	    mountains.
74	
75	    If the view of a pixel at location (lat, lon) is blocked by a cloud
76	    at height h, this function calculates the (lat, lon) coordinates
77	    of the cloud above/in front of the invisible surface.
78	
79	    For scenes that are only partly cloudy, the user might set the cloud top
80	    height for clear-sky pixels to NaN.  This function will return a corrected
81	    lat/lon as NaN as well.  The user can use the original lat/lon for those
82	    pixels or use the higher level :class:`ParallaxCorrection` class.
83	
84	    This function assumes a spherical Earth.
85	
86	    .. note::
87	
88	        Be careful with units!  This code expects ``sat_alt`` and
89	        ``height`` to be in meter above the Earth's surface.  You may
90	        have to convert your input correspondingly.  Cloud Top Height
91	        is usually reported in meters above the Earth's surface, rarely
92	        in km.  Satellite altitude may be reported in either m or km, but
93	        orbital parameters are usually in relation to the Earth's centre.
94	        The Earth radius from pyresample is reported in km.
95	
96	    Args:
97	        sat_lon (numbers.Number): Satellite longitude in geodetic coordinates [degrees]
98	        sat_lat (numbers.Number): Satellite latitude in geodetic coordinates [degrees]
99	        sat_alt (numbers.Number): Satellite altitude above the Earth surface [m]
100	        lon (dask.array.Array or numbers.Number): Longitudes of pixel or pixels to be corrected,
101	            in geodetic coordinates [degrees]
102	        lat (dask.array.Array or numbers.Number): Latitudes of pixel/pixels to be corrected, in
103	            geodetic coordinates [degrees]
104	        height (dask.array.Array or numbers.Number): Heights of pixels on which the correction
105	            will be based.  Typically this is the cloud top height. [m]
106	
107	    Returns:
108	        tuple[float, float]: Corrected geolocation
109	            Corrected geolocation ``(lon, lat)`` in geodetic coordinates for
110	            the pixel(s) to be corrected. [degrees]
111	    """
112	    elevation = _get_satellite_elevation(sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt, lon, lat)
113	    parallax_distance = _calculate_slant_cloud_distance(height, elevation)
114	    shifted_xyz = _get_parallax_shift_xyz(
115	            sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt, lon, lat, parallax_distance)
116	
117	    return xyz2lonlat(
118	        shifted_xyz[..., 0], shifted_xyz[..., 1], shifted_xyz[..., 2])
119

121	def get_surface_parallax_displacement(
122	        sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt, lon, lat, height):
123	    """Calculate surface parallax displacement.
124	
125	    Calculate the displacement due to parallax error.  Input parameters are
126	    identical to :func:`get_parallax_corrected_lonlats`.
127	
128	    Returns:
129	        (numbers.Number, dask.array.Array): parallax displacement in meters
130	    """
131	    (corr_lon, corr_lat) = get_parallax_corrected_lonlats(sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt, lon, lat, height)
132	    # Get parallax displacement
133	    geod = Geod(ellps="sphere")
134	    _, _, parallax_dist = geod.inv(corr_lon, corr_lat, lon, lat)
135	    return parallax_dist

138	def _get_parallax_shift_xyz(sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt, lon, lat, parallax_distance):
139	    """Calculate the parallax shift in cartesian coordinates.
140	
141	    From satellite position and cloud position, get the parallax shift in
142	    cartesian coordinates:
143	
144	    Args:
145	        sat_lon (numbers.Number): Satellite longitude in geodetic coordinates [degrees]
146	        sat_lat (numbers.Number): Satellite latitude in geodetic coordinates [degrees]
147	        sat_alt (numbers.Number): Satellite altitude above the Earth surface [m]
148	        lon (dask.array.Array or numbers.Number): Longitudes of pixel or pixels to be corrected,
149	            in geodetic coordinates [degrees]
150	        lat (dask.array.Array or numbers.Number): Latitudes of pixel/pixels to be corrected, in
151	            geodetic coordinates [degrees]
152	        parallax_distance (dask.array.Array or numbers.Number): Cloud to ground distance with parallax
153	            effect [m].
154	
155	    Returns:
156	        Parallax shift in cartesian coordinates in meter.
157	    """
158	    sat_xyz = np.hstack(lonlat2xyz(sat_lon, sat_lat)) * sat_alt
159	    cth_xyz = np.stack(lonlat2xyz(lon, lat), axis=-1) * EARTH_RADIUS*1e3  # km → m
160	    delta_xyz = cth_xyz - sat_xyz
161	    sat_distance = np.sqrt((delta_xyz*delta_xyz).sum(axis=-1))
162	    dist_shape = delta_xyz.shape[:-1] + (1,)  # force correct array broadcasting
163	    return cth_xyz - delta_xyz*(parallax_distance/sat_distance).reshape(dist_shape)
164

166	def _get_satellite_elevation(sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt, lon, lat):
167	    """Get satellite elevation.
168	
169	    Get the satellite elevation from satellite lon/lat/alt for positions
170	    lon/lat.
171	    """
172	    placeholder_date = datetime.datetime(2000, 1, 1)  # no impact on get_observer_look?
173	    (_, elevation) = get_observer_look(
174	            sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt/1e3,  # m → km (wanted by get_observer_look)
175	            placeholder_date, lon, lat, 0)
176	    return elevation

179	def _calculate_slant_cloud_distance(height, elevation):
180	    """Calculate slant cloud to ground distance.
181	
182	    From (cloud top) height and satellite elevation, calculate the
183	    slant cloud-to-ground distance along the line of sight of the satellite.
184	    """
185	    if np.isscalar(elevation) and elevation == 0:
186	        raise NotImplementedError(
187	                "Parallax correction not implemented for "
188	                "satellite elevation 0")
189	    if np.isscalar(elevation) and elevation < 0:
190	        raise ValueError(
191	                "Satellite is below the horizon.  Cannot calculate parallax "
192	                "correction.")
193	    return height / np.sin(np.deg2rad(elevation))

196	class ParallaxCorrection:
197	    """Parallax correction calculations.
198	
199	    This class contains higher-level functionality to wrap the parallax
200	    correction calculations in :func:`get_parallax_corrected_lonlats`.  The class is
201	    initialised using a base area, which is the area for which a corrected
202	    geolocation will be calculated.  The resulting object is a callable.
203	    Calling the object with an array of (cloud top) heights returns a
204	    :class:`~pyresample.geometry.SwathDefinition` describing the new ,
205	    corrected geolocation.  The cloud top height should cover at least the
206	    area for which the corrected geolocation will be calculated.
207	
208	    Note that the ``ctth`` dataset must contain satellite location
209	    metadata, such as set in the ``orbital_parameters`` dataset attribute
210	    that is set by many Satpy readers.  It is essential that the datasets to be
211	    corrected are coming from the same platform as the provided cloud top
212	    height.
213	
214	    A note on the algorithm and the implementation.  Parallax correction
215	    is inherently an inverse problem.  The reported geolocation in
216	    satellite data files is the true location plus the parallax error.
217	    Therefore, this class first calculates the true geolocation (using
218	    :func:`get_parallax_corrected_lonlats`), which gives a shifted longitude and
219	    shifted latitude on an irregular grid.  The difference between
220	    the original and the shifted grid is the parallax error or shift.
221	    The magnitude of this error can be estimated with
222	    :func:`get_surface_parallax_displacement`.
223	    With this difference, we need to invert the parallax correction to
224	    calculate the corrected geolocation.  Due to parallax correction,
225	    high clouds shift a lot, low clouds shift a little, and cloud-free
226	    pixels shift not at all.  The shift may result in zero, one,
227	    two, or more source pixel onto a destination pixel.  Physically,
228	    this corresponds to the situation where a narrow but high cloud is
229	    viewed at a large angle.  The cloud may occupy two or more pixels when
230	    viewed at a large angle, but only one when viewed straight from above.
231	    To accurately reproduce this perspective, the parallax correction uses
232	    the :class:`~pyresample.bucket.BucketResampler` class, specifically
233	    the :meth:`~pyresample.bucket.BucketResampler.get_abs_max` method, to
234	    retain only the largest absolute shift (corresponding to the highest
235	    cloud) within each pixel.  Any other resampling method at this step
236	    would yield incorrect results.  When cloud moves over clear-sky, the
237	    clear-sky pixel is unshifted and the shift is located exactly in the
238	    centre of the grid box, so nearest-neighbour resampling would lead to
239	    such shifts being deselected.  Other resampling methods would average
240	    large shifts with small shifts, leading to unpredictable results.
241	    Now the reprojected shifts can be applied to the original lat/lon,
242	    returning a new :class:`~pyresample.geometry.SwathDefinition`.
243	    This is is the object returned by :meth:`corrected_area`.
244	
245	    This procedure can be configured as a modifier using the
246	    :class:`ParallaxCorrectionModifier` class.  However, the modifier can only
247	    be applied to one dataset at the time, which may not provide optimal
248	    performance, although dask should reuse identical calculations between
249	    multiple channels.
250	
251	    """
252	
253	    def __init__(self, base_area,
254	                 debug_mode=False):
255	        """Initialise parallax correction class.
256	
257	        Args:
258	            base_area (pyresample.geometry.AreaDefinition): Area for which calculated
259	                geolocation will be calculated.
260	            debug_mode (bool): Store diagnostic information in
261	                self.diagnostics.  This attribute always apply to the most
262	                recently applied operation only.
263	        """
264	        self.base_area = base_area
265	        self.debug_mode = debug_mode
266	        self.diagnostics = {}
267	
268	    def __call__(self, cth_dataset, **kwargs):  # noqa: D417
269	        """Apply parallax correction to dataset.
270	
271	        Args:
272	            cth_dataset: Dataset containing cloud top heights (or other heights
273	                to be corrected).
274	
275	        Returns:
276	            :class:'~pyresample.geometry.SwathDefinition`: Swathdefinition with corrected
277	                lat/lon coordinates.
278	        """
279	        self.diagnostics.clear()
280	        return self.corrected_area(cth_dataset, **kwargs)
281	
282	    def corrected_area(self, cth_dataset,
283	                       cth_resampler="nearest",
284	                       cth_radius_of_influence=50000,
285	                       lonlat_chunks=1024):
286	        """Return the parallax corrected SwathDefinition.
287	
288	        Using the cloud top heights provided in ``cth_dataset``, calculate the
289	        :class:`pyresample.geometry.SwathDefinition` that estimates the
290	        geolocation for each pixel if it had been viewed from straight above
291	        (without parallax error).  The cloud top height will first be resampled
292	        onto the area passed upon class initialisation in :meth:`__init__`.
293	        Pixels that are invisible after parallax correction are not retained
294	        but get geolocation NaN.
295	
296	        Args:
297	            cth_dataset (xarray.DataArray): Cloud top height in
298	                meters.  The variable attributes must contain an ``area``
299	                attribute describing the geolocation in a pyresample-aware way,
300	                and they must contain satellite orbital parameters.  The
301	                dimensions must be ``(y, x)``.  For best performance, this
302	                should be a dask-based :class:`~xarray.DataArray`.
303	            cth_resampler (str, Optional): Resampler to use when resampling the
304	                (cloud top) height to the base area.  Defaults to "nearest".
305	            cth_radius_of_influence (numbers.Number, Optional): Radius of influence to use when
306	                resampling the (cloud top) height to the base area.  Defaults
307	                to 50000.
308	            lonlat_chunks (int, Optional): Chunking to use when calculating lon/lats.
309	                Probably the default (1024) should be fine.
310	
311	        Returns:
312	            :class:`~pyresample.geometry.SwathDefinition` describing parallax
313	            corrected geolocation.
314	        """
315	        logger.debug("Calculating parallax correction using heights from "
316	                     f"{cth_dataset.attrs.get('name', cth_dataset.name)!s}, "
317	                     f"with base area {self.base_area.name!s}.")
318	        (sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt_m) = _get_satpos_from_cth(cth_dataset)
319	        self._check_overlap(cth_dataset)
320	
321	        cth_dataset = self._prepare_cth_dataset(
322	                cth_dataset, resampler=cth_resampler,
323	                radius_of_influence=cth_radius_of_influence,
324	                lonlat_chunks=lonlat_chunks)
325	
326	        (base_lon, base_lat) = self.base_area.get_lonlats(chunks=lonlat_chunks)
327	        # calculate the shift/error due to the parallax effect
328	        (corrected_lon, corrected_lat) = get_parallax_corrected_lonlats(
329	                sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt_m,
330	                base_lon, base_lat, cth_dataset.data)
331	
332	        shifted_area = self._get_swathdef_from_lon_lat(corrected_lon, corrected_lat)
333	
334	        # But we are not actually moving pixels, rather we want a
335	        # coordinate transformation. With this transformation we approximately
336	        # invert the pixel coordinate transformation, giving the lon and lat
337	        # where we should retrieve a value for a given pixel.
338	        (proj_lon, proj_lat) = self._get_corrected_lon_lat(
339	                base_lon, base_lat, shifted_area)
340	
341	        return self._get_swathdef_from_lon_lat(proj_lon, proj_lat)
342	
343	    @staticmethod
344	    def _get_swathdef_from_lon_lat(lon, lat):
345	        """Return a SwathDefinition from lon/lat.
346	
347	        Turn ndarrays describing lon/lat into xarray with dimensions y, x, then
348	        use these to create a :class:`~pyresample.geometry.SwathDefinition`.
349	        """
350	        # lons and lats passed to SwathDefinition must be data arrays with
351	        # dimensions.
352	        return SwathDefinition(
353	            xr.DataArray(lon, dims=("y", "x")),
354	            xr.DataArray(lat, dims=("y", "x")))
355	
356	    def _prepare_cth_dataset(
357	            self, cth_dataset, resampler="nearest", radius_of_influence=50000,
358	            lonlat_chunks=1024):
359	        """Prepare CTH dataset.
360	
361	        Set cloud top height to zero wherever lat/lon are valid but CTH is
362	        undefined.  Then resample onto the base area.
363	        """
364	        # for calculating the parallax effect, set cth to 0 where it is
365	        # undefined, unless pixels have no valid lat/lon
366	        # NB: 0 may be below the surface... could be a problem for high
367	        # resolution imagery in mountainous or high elevation terrain
368	        # NB: how tolerant of xarray & dask is this?
369	        resampled_cth_dataset = resample_dataset(
370	                cth_dataset, self.base_area, resampler=resampler,
371	                radius_of_influence=radius_of_influence)
372	        (pixel_lon, pixel_lat) = resampled_cth_dataset.attrs["area"].get_lonlats(
373	                chunks=lonlat_chunks)
374	        masked_resampled_cth_dataset = resampled_cth_dataset.where(
375	                np.isfinite(pixel_lon) & np.isfinite(pixel_lat))
376	        masked_resampled_cth_dataset = masked_resampled_cth_dataset.where(
377	                masked_resampled_cth_dataset.notnull(), 0)
378	        return masked_resampled_cth_dataset
379	
380	    def _check_overlap(self, cth_dataset):
381	        """Ensure cth_dataset is usable for parallax correction.
382	
383	        Checks the coverage of ``cth_dataset`` compared to the ``base_area``.  If
384	        the entirety of ``base_area`` is covered by ``cth_dataset``, do
385	        nothing.  If only part of ``base_area`` is covered by ``cth_dataset``,
386	        raise a `IncompleteHeightWarning`.  If none of ``base_area`` is covered
387	        by ``cth_dataset``, raise a `MissingHeightError`.
388	        """
389	        warnings.warn(
390	            "Overlap checking is not available in the reduced dependency path.",
391	            stacklevel=3
392	        )
393	
394	    def _get_corrected_lon_lat(self, base_lon, base_lat, shifted_area):
395	        """Calculate the corrected lon/lat based from the shifted area.
396	
397	        After calculating the shifted area based on
398	        :func:`get_parallax_corrected_lonlats`,
399	        we invert the parallax error and estimate where those pixels came from.
400	        For details on the algorithm, see the class docstring.
401	        """
402	        (corrected_lon, corrected_lat) = shifted_area.get_lonlats(chunks=1024)
403	        lon_diff = corrected_lon - base_lon
404	        lat_diff = corrected_lat - base_lat
405	        # We use the bucket resampler here, because parallax correction
406	        # inevitably means there will be 2 source pixels ending up in the same
407	        # destination pixel.  We want to choose the biggest shift (max abs in
408	        # lat_diff and lon_diff), because the biggest shift corresponds to the
409	        # highest clouds, and if we move a 10 km cloud over a 2 km one, we
410	        # should retain the 10 km.
411	        #
412	        # some things to keep in mind:
413	        # - even with a constant cloud height, 3 source pixels may end up in
414	        #   the same destination pixel, because pixels get larger in the
415	        #   direction of the satellite.  This means clouds may shrink as they
416	        #   approach the satellite.
417	        # - the x-shift is a function of y and the y-shift is a function of x,
418	        #   so a cloud that was rectangular at the start may no longer be
419	        #   rectangular at the end
420	        bur = BucketResampler(self.base_area,
421	                              da.array(corrected_lon), da.array(corrected_lat))
422	        inv_lat_diff = bur.get_abs_max(lat_diff)
423	        inv_lon_diff = bur.get_abs_max(lon_diff)
424	
425	        inv_lon = base_lon - inv_lon_diff
426	        inv_lat = base_lat - inv_lat_diff
427	        if self.debug_mode:
428	            self.diagnostics["corrected_lon"] = corrected_lon
429	            self.diagnostics["corrected_lat"] = corrected_lat
430	            self.diagnostics["inv_lon"] = inv_lon
431	            self.diagnostics["inv_lat"] = inv_lat
432	            self.diagnostics["inv_lon_diff"] = inv_lon_diff
433	            self.diagnostics["inv_lat_diff"] = inv_lat_diff
434	            self.diagnostics["base_lon"] = base_lon
435	            self.diagnostics["base_lat"] = base_lat
436	            self.diagnostics["lon_diff"] = lon_diff
437	            self.diagnostics["lat_diff"] = lat_diff
438	            self.diagnostics["shifted_area"] = shifted_area
439	            self.diagnostics["count"] = xr.DataArray(
440	                bur.get_count(), dims=("y", "x"), attrs={"area": self.base_area})
441	        return (inv_lon, inv_lat)

444	class ParallaxCorrectionModifier(ModifierBase):
445	    """Modifier for parallax correction.
446	
447	    Apply parallax correction as a modifier.  Uses the
448	    :class:`ParallaxCorrection` class, which in turn uses the
449	    :func:`get_parallax_corrected_lonlats` function.  See the documentation there for
450	    details on the behaviour.
451	
452	    To use this, add to ``composites/visir.yaml`` within ``SATPY_CONFIG_PATH``
453	    something like::
454	
455	        sensor_name: visir
456	
457	        modifiers:
458	          parallax_corrected:
459	            modifier: !!python/name:satpy.modifiers.parallax.ParallaxCorrectionModifier
460	            prerequisites:
461	              - "ctth_alti"
462	            dataset_radius_of_influence: 50000
463	
464	        composites:
465	
466	          parallax_corrected_VIS006:
467	            compositor: !!python/name:satpy.composites.SingleBandCompositor
468	            prerequisites:
469	              - name: VIS006
470	                modifiers: [parallax_corrected]
471	
472	    Here, ``ctth_alti`` is CTH provided by the ``nwcsaf-geo`` reader, so to use it
473	    one would have to pass both on scene creation::
474	
475	        sc = Scene({"seviri_l1b_hrit": files_l1b, "nwcsaf-geo": files_l2})
476	        sc.load(["parallax_corrected_VIS006"])
477	
478	    The modifier takes optional global parameters, all of which are optional.
479	    They affect various steps in the algorithm.  Setting them may impact
480	    performance:
481	
482	    cth_resampler
483	        Resampler to use when resampling (cloud top) height to the base area.
484	        Defaults to "nearest".
485	    cth_radius_of_influence
486	        Radius of influence to use when resampling the (cloud top) height to
487	        the base area.  Defaults to 50000.
488	    lonlat_chunks
489	        Chunk size to use when obtaining longitudes and latitudes from the area
490	        definition.  Defaults to 1024.  If you set this to None, then parallax
491	        correction will involve premature calculation.  Changing this may or
492	        may not make parallax correction slower or faster.
493	    dataset_radius_of_influence
494	        Radius of influence to use when resampling the dataset onto the
495	        swathdefinition describing the parallax-corrected area.  Defaults to
496	        50000.  This always uses nearest neighbour resampling.
497	
498	    Alternately, you can use the lower-level API directly with the
499	    :class:`ParallaxCorrection` class, which may be more efficient if multiple
500	    datasets need to be corrected.  RGB Composites cannot be modified in this way
501	    (i.e. you can't replace "VIS006" by "natural_color").  To get a parallax
502	    corrected RGB composite, create a new composite where each input has the
503	    modifier applied.  The parallax calculation should only occur once, because
504	    calculations are happening via dask and dask should reuse the calculation.
505	    """
506	
507	    def __call__(self, projectables, optional_datasets=None, **info):
508	        """Apply parallax correction.
509	
510	        The argument ``projectables`` needs to contain the dataset to be
511	        projected and the height to use for the correction.
512	        """
513	        (to_be_corrected, cth) = projectables
514	        base_area = to_be_corrected.attrs["area"]
515	        corrector = self._get_corrector(base_area)
516	        plax_corr_area = corrector(
517	                cth,
518	                cth_resampler=self.attrs.get("cth_resampler", "nearest"),
519	                cth_radius_of_influence=self.attrs.get("cth_radius_of_influence", 50_000),
520	                lonlat_chunks=self.attrs.get("lonlat_chunks", 1024),
521	                )
522	        res = resample_dataset(
523	                to_be_corrected, plax_corr_area,
524	                radius_of_influence=self.attrs.get("dataset_radius_of_influence", 50_000),
525	                fill_value=np.nan)
526	        res.attrs["area"] = to_be_corrected.attrs["area"]
527	        self.apply_modifier_info(to_be_corrected, res)
528	
529	        return res
530	
531	    def _get_corrector(self, base_area):
532	        # only pass on those attributes that are arguments by
533	        # ParallaxCorrection.__init__
534	        sig = inspect.signature(ParallaxCorrection.__init__)
535	        kwargs = {}
536	        for k in sig.parameters.keys() & self.attrs.keys():
537	            kwargs[k] = self.attrs[k]
538	        corrector = ParallaxCorrection(base_area, **kwargs)
539	        return corrector

542	def _get_satpos_from_cth(cth_dataset):
543	    """Obtain satellite position from CTH dataset, height in meter.
544	
545	    From a CTH dataset, obtain the satellite position lon, lat, altitude/m,
546	    either directly from orbital parameters, or, when missing, from the
547	    platform name using pyorbital and skyfield.
548	    """
549	    (sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt_km) = get_satpos(
550	            cth_dataset, use_tle=True)
551	    return (sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt_km * 1000)

279	def atmospheric_path_length_correction(data, cos_zen, limit=88., max_sza=95.):
280	    """Perform Sun zenith angle correction.
281	
282	    This function uses the correction method proposed by
283	    Li and Shibata (2006): https://doi.org/10.1175/JAS3682.1
284	
285	    The correction is limited to ``limit`` degrees (default: 88.0 degrees). For
286	    larger zenith angles, the correction is the same as at the ``limit`` if
287	    ``max_sza`` is `None`. The default behavior is to gradually reduce the
288	    correction past ``limit`` degrees up to ``max_sza`` where the correction
289	    becomes 0. Both ``data`` and ``cos_zen`` should be 2D arrays of the same
290	    shape.
291	
292	    """
293	    # Convert the zenith angle limit to cosine of zenith angle
294	    limit_rad = np.deg2rad(limit)
295	    limit_cos = np.cos(limit_rad)
296	    max_sza_rad = np.deg2rad(max_sza) if max_sza is not None else max_sza
297	
298	    # Cosine correction
299	    corr = _get_sunz_corr_li_and_shibata(cos_zen)
300	    # Use constant value (the limit) for larger zenith angles
301	    corr_lim = _get_sunz_corr_li_and_shibata(limit_cos)
302	
303	    if max_sza is not None:
304	        # gradually fall off for larger zenith angle
305	        grad_factor = (np.arccos(cos_zen) - limit_rad) / (max_sza_rad - limit_rad)
306	        # invert the factor so maximum correction is done at `limit` and falls off later
307	        grad_factor = 1. - np.log(grad_factor + 1) / np.log(2)
308	        # make sure we don't make anything negative
309	        grad_factor = grad_factor.clip(0.)
310	    else:
311	        # Use constant value (the limit) for larger zenith angles
312	        grad_factor = 1.
313	    corr = corr.where(cos_zen > limit_cos, grad_factor * corr_lim)
314	    # Force "night" pixels to 0 (where SZA is invalid)
315	    corr = corr.where(cos_zen.notnull(), 0)
316	
317	    return data * corr

412	def _get_satpos_from_platform_name(cth_dataset):
413	    """Get satellite position if no orbital parameters in metadata.
414	
415	    Some cloud top height datasets lack orbital parameter information in
416	    metadata.  Here, orbital parameters are calculated based on the platform
417	    name and start time, via Two Line Element (TLE) information.
418	
419	    Needs pyorbital, skyfield, and astropy to be installed.
420	    """
421	    from skyfield.api import EarthSatellite, load
422	    from skyfield.toposlib import wgs84
423	    from satpy.tle_catalogue import read
424	
425	    name = cth_dataset.attrs["platform_name"]
426	    tle = read(name)
427	    es = EarthSatellite(tle.line1, tle.line2, name)
428	    ts = load.timescale(builtin=True)
429	    gc = es.at(ts.from_datetime(
430	        cth_dataset.attrs["start_time"].replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)))
431	    (lat, lon) = wgs84.latlon_of(gc)
432	    height = wgs84.height_of(gc).to("km")
433	    return (lon.degrees, lat.degrees, height.value)

def get_observer_look(sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt, utc_time, lon, lat, alt):
    """Calculate observers look angle to a satellite.

    http://celestrak.com/columns/v02n02/

    :utc_time: Observation time (datetime object)
    :lon: Longitude of observer position on ground in degrees east
    :lat: Latitude of observer position on ground in degrees north
    :alt: Altitude above sea-level (geoid) of observer position on ground in km

    :return: (Azimuth, Elevation)
    """
    (pos_x, pos_y, pos_z), (vel_x, vel_y, vel_z) = astronomy.observer_position(
        utc_time, sat_lon, sat_lat, sat_alt)

    (opos_x, opos_y, opos_z), (ovel_x, ovel_y, ovel_z) = \
        astronomy.observer_position(utc_time, lon, lat, alt)

    lon = np.deg2rad(lon)
    lat = np.deg2rad(lat)

    theta = (astronomy.gmst(utc_time) + lon) % (2 * np.pi)

    rx = pos_x - opos_x
    ry = pos_y - opos_y
    rz = pos_z - opos_z

    sin_lat = np.sin(lat)
    cos_lat = np.cos(lat)
    sin_theta = np.sin(theta)
    cos_theta = np.cos(theta)

    top_s = sin_lat * cos_theta * rx + \
        sin_lat * sin_theta * ry - cos_lat * rz
    top_e = -sin_theta * rx + cos_theta * ry
    top_z = cos_lat * cos_theta * rx + \
        cos_lat * sin_theta * ry + sin_lat * rz

    # Azimuth is undefined when elevation is 90 degrees, 180 (pi) will be returned.
    az_ = np.arctan2(-top_e, top_s) + np.pi
    az_ = np.mod(az_, 2 * np.pi)  # Needed on some platforms

    rg_ = np.sqrt(rx * rx + ry * ry + rz * rz)

    top_z_divided_by_rg_ = top_z / rg_

    # Due to rounding top_z can be larger than rg_ (when el_ ~ 90).
    top_z_divided_by_rg_ = top_z_divided_by_rg_.clip(max=1)
    el_ = np.arcsin(top_z_divided_by_rg_)

    return np.rad2deg(az_), np.rad2deg(el_)

def observer_position(utc_time, lon, lat, alt):
    """Calculate observer ECI position.

    http://celestrak.com/columns/v02n03/
    """
    lon = np.deg2rad(lon)
    lat = np.deg2rad(lat)

    theta = (gmst(utc_time) + lon) % (2 * np.pi)
    c = 1 / np.sqrt(1 + F * (F - 2) * np.sin(lat)**2)
    sq = c * (1 - F)**2

    achcp = (A * c + alt) * np.cos(lat)
    x = achcp * np.cos(theta)  # kilometers
    y = achcp * np.sin(theta)
    z = (A * sq + alt) * np.sin(lat)

    vx = -MFACTOR * y  # kilometers/second
    vy = MFACTOR * x
    vz = _float_to_sibling_result(0.0, vx)

    if not isinstance(lon, float):
        x = x.astype(lon.dtype, copy=False)
        y = y.astype(lon.dtype, copy=False)
        z = z.astype(lon.dtype, copy=False)
        vx = vx.astype(lon.dtype, copy=False)
        vy = vy.astype(lon.dtype, copy=False)
        vz = vz.astype(lon.dtype, copy=False)  # type: ignore[union-attr]

result.text:
class BucketResampler(object):
    """Bucket resampler.

    Bucket resampling is useful for calculating averages and hit-counts
    when aggregating data to coarser scale grids.

    Below are examples how to use the resampler.

    Read data using Satpy.  The resampling can also be done (apart from
    fractions) directly from Satpy, but this demonstrates the direct
    low-level usage.

    >>> from pyresample.bucket import BucketResampler
    >>> from satpy import Scene
    >>> from satpy.resample import get_area_def
    >>> fname = "hrpt_noaa19_20170519_1214_42635.l1b"
    >>> glbl = Scene(filenames=[fname])
    >>> glbl.load(['4'])
    >>> data = glbl['4']
    >>> lons, lats = data.area.get_lonlats()
    >>> target_area = get_area_def('euro4')

    Initialize the resampler

    >>> resampler = BucketResampler(target_area, lons, lats)

    Calculate the sum of all the data in each grid location:

    >>> sums = resampler.get_sum(data)

    Calculate how many values were collected at each grid location:

    >>> counts = resampler.get_count()

    The average can be calculated from the above two results, or directly
    using the helper method:

    >>> average = resampler.get_average(data)

    Calculate fractions of occurrences of different values in each grid
    location.  The data needs to be categorical (in integers), so
    we'll create some categorical data from the brightness temperature
    data that were read earlier.  The data are returned in a
    dictionary with the categories as keys.

    >>> data = da.where(data > 250, 1, 0)
    >>> fractions = resampler.get_fractions(data, categories=[0, 1])
    >>> import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    >>> plt.imshow(fractions[0]); plt.show()
    """

    def __init__(self, target_area, source_lons, source_lats):
        self.target_area = target_area
        self.source_lons = source_lons
        self.source_lats = source_lats
        self.prj = Proj(self.target_area.proj_dict)
        self.x_idxs = None
        self.y_idxs = None
        self.idxs = None
        self._get_indices()
        self.counts = None

    def _get_proj_coordinates(self, lons, lats):
        """Calculate projection coordinates.

        Parameters
        ----------
        lons : Numpy or Dask array
            Longitude coordinates
        lats : Numpy or Dask array
            Latitude coordinates
        """
        proj_x, proj_y = self.prj(lons, lats)
        return np.stack((proj_x, proj_y))

    def _get_indices(self):
        """Calculate projection indices.

        Returns
        -------
        x_idxs : Dask array
            X indices of the target grid where the data are put
        y_idxs : Dask array
            Y indices of the target grid where the data are put
        """
        LOG.info("Determine bucket resampling indices")

        # Transform source lons/lats to target projection coordinates x/y
        lons = self.source_lons.ravel()
        lats = self.source_lats.ravel()
        result = da.map_blocks(self._get_proj_coordinates, lons, lats,
                               meta=np.array((), dtype=lons.dtype),
                               dtype=lons.dtype,
                               new_axis=0, chunks=(2,) + lons.chunks)
        proj_x = result[0, :]
        proj_y = result[1, :]

        # Calculate array indices. Orient so that 0-meridian is pointing down.
        adef = self.target_area
        x_res, y_res = adef.resolution
        x_idxs = da.floor((proj_x - adef.area_extent[0]) / x_res).astype(np.int64)
        y_idxs = da.floor((adef.area_extent[3] - proj_y) / y_res).astype(np.int64)

        # Get valid index locations
        mask = (x_idxs >= 0) & (x_idxs < adef.width) & (y_idxs >= 0) & (y_idxs < adef.height)
        self.y_idxs = da.where(mask, y_idxs, -1)
        self.x_idxs = da.where(mask, x_idxs, -1)

        # Convert X- and Y-indices to raveled indexing
        target_shape = self.target_area.shape
        self.idxs = self.y_idxs * target_shape[1] + self.x_idxs

    def get_sum(self, data, fill_value=np.nan, skipna=True, empty_bucket_value=0):
        """Calculate sums for each bin with drop-in-a-bucket resampling.

        Parameters
        ----------
        data : Numpy or Dask array
            Data to be binned and summed.
        fill_value : float
            Fill value of the input data marking missing/invalid values.
            Default: np.nan
        skipna : boolean (optional)
            If True, skips missing values (as marked by NaN or `fill_value`) for the sum calculation
            (similarly to Numpy's `nansum`). Buckets containing only missing values are set to `empty_bucket_value`.
            If False, sets the bucket to fill_value if one or more missing values are present in the bucket
            (similarly to Numpy's `sum`).
            In both cases, empty buckets are set to `empty_bucket_value`.
            Default: True
        empty_bucket_value : float
            Set empty buckets to the given value. Empty buckets are considered as the buckets with value 0.
            Note that a bucket could become 0 as the result of a sum
            of positive and negative values. If the user needs to identify these zero-buckets reliably,
            `get_count()` can be used for this purpose.
            Default: 0

        Returns
        -------
        data : Numpy or Dask array
            Bin-wise sums in the target grid
        """
        LOG.info("Get sum of values in each location")

        if isinstance(data, xr.DataArray):
            data = data.data
        data = data.ravel()

        # Remove fill_values values from the data when used as weights
        invalid_mask = _get_invalid_mask(data, fill_value)
        weights = da.where(invalid_mask, 0, data)

        # Rechunk indices to match the data chunking
        if weights.chunks != self.idxs.chunks:
            self.idxs = da.rechunk(self.idxs, weights.chunks)

        # Calculate the sum of the data falling to each bin
        out_size = self.target_area.size
        sums, _ = da.histogram(self.idxs, bins=out_size, range=(0, out_size),
                               weights=weights, density=False)

        # TODO remove following line in favour of weights = data when dask histogram bug (issue #6935) is fixed
        sums = self._mask_bins_with_nan_if_not_skipna(skipna, data, out_size, sums, fill_value)

        if empty_bucket_value != 0:
            sums = da.where(sums == 0, empty_bucket_value, sums)

        return sums.reshape(self.target_area.shape)

    def _mask_bins_with_nan_if_not_skipna(self, skipna, data, out_size, statistic, fill_value):
        if not skipna:
            missing_val = _get_invalid_mask(data, fill_value)
            missing_val_bins, _ = da.histogram(self.idxs[missing_val], bins=out_size,
                                               range=(0, out_size))
            statistic = da.where(missing_val_bins > 0, fill_value, statistic)
        return statistic

    def _call_bin_statistic(self, statistic_method, data, fill_value=None, skipna=None):
        """Calculate statistics (min/max) for each bin with drop-in-a-bucket resampling."""
        if isinstance(data, xr.DataArray):
            data = data.data
        data = data.ravel()

        # Rechunk indices to match the data chunking
        if data.chunks != self.idxs.chunks:
            self.idxs = da.rechunk(self.idxs, data.chunks)

        out_shape = self.target_area.shape

        statistics = da.from_delayed(
            _get_statistics(statistic_method, data, self.idxs, out_shape),
            shape=out_shape,
            dtype=np.float64)

        return statistics

    def get_min(self, data, fill_value=np.nan, skipna=True):
        """Calculate minimums for each bin with drop-in-a-bucket resampling.

        Parameters
        ----------
        data : Numpy or Dask array
            Data to be binned.
        skipna : boolean (optional)
                If True, skips NaN values for the minimum calculation
                (similarly to Numpy's `nanmin`). Buckets containing only NaN are set to zero.
                If False, sets the bucket to NaN if one or more NaN values are present in the bucket
                (similarly to Numpy's `min`).
                In both cases, empty buckets are set to 0.
                Default: True

        Returns
        -------
        data : Numpy or Dask array
            Bin-wise minimums in the target grid
        """
        LOG.info("Get min of values in each location")
        return self._call_bin_statistic('min', data, fill_value, skipna)

    def get_max(self, data, fill_value=np.nan, skipna=True):
        """Calculate maximums for each bin with drop-in-a-bucket resampling.

        Parameters
        ----------
        data : Numpy or Dask array
            Data to be binned.
        skipna : boolean (optional)
                If True, skips NaN values for the maximum calculation
                (similarly to Numpy's `nanmax`). Buckets containing only NaN are set to zero.
                If False, sets the bucket to NaN if one or more NaN values are present in the bucket
                (similarly to Numpy's `max`).
                In both cases, empty buckets are set to 0.
                Default: True

        Returns
        -------
        data : Numpy or Dask array
            Bin-wise maximums in the target grid
        """
        LOG.info("Get max of values in each location")
        return self._call_bin_statistic('max', data, fill_value, skipna)

    def get_abs_max(self, data, fill_value=np.nan, skipna=True):
        """Calculate absolute maximums for each bin with drop-in-a-bucket resampling.

        Returns for each bin the original signed value which has the largest
        absolute value.

        .. warning::

            The slow :meth:`pandas.DataFrame.groupby` method is temporarily used here,
            as the `dask_groupby <https://github.com/dcherian/dask_groupby>`_ is still under development.

        Parameters
        ----------
        data : Numpy or Dask array
            Data to be binned.
        fill_value : number (optional)
            Value to use for empty buckets or all-NaN buckets.
        skipna : boolean (optional)
            If True, skips NaN values for the maximum calculation
            (similarly to Numpy's `nanmax`). Buckets containing only NaN are
            set to fill value.
            If False, sets the bucket to NaN if one or more NaN values are present in the bucket
            (similarly to Numpy's `max`).
            In both cases, empty buckets are set to fill value.
            Default: True

        Returns
        -------
        data : Numpy or Dask array
            Bin-wise maximums in the target grid
        """
        max_ = self.get_max(data, fill_value=fill_value, skipna=skipna)
        min_ = self.get_min(data, fill_value=fill_value, skipna=skipna)
        return self._get_abs_max_from_min_max(min_, max_)

    @staticmethod
    def _get_abs_max_from_min_max(min_, max_):
        """From array of min and array of max, get array of abs max."""
        return da.where(-min_ > max_, min_, max_)

    def get_count(self):
        """Count the number of occurrences for each bin using drop-in-a-bucket resampling.

        Returns
        -------
        data : Dask array
            Bin-wise count of hits for each target grid location
        """
        LOG.info("Get number of values in each location")

        out_size = self.target_area.size

        # Calculate the sum of the data falling to each bin
        if self.counts is None:
            counts, _ = da.histogram(self.idxs, bins=out_size,
                                     range=(0, out_size))
            self.counts = counts.reshape(self.target_area.shape)

        return self.counts

    def get_average(self, data, fill_value=np.nan, skipna=True):
        """Calculate bin-averages using bucket resampling.

        Parameters
        ----------
        data : Numpy or Dask array
            Data to be binned and averaged.
        fill_value : float
            Fill value to mark missing/invalid values in the input data,
            as well as in the binned and averaged output data.
            Default: np.nan
        skipna : bool
            If True, skips missing values (as marked by NaN or `fill_value`) for the average calculation
            (similarly to Numpy's `nanmean`). Buckets containing only missing values are set to fill_value.
            If False, sets the bucket to fill_value if one or more missing values are present in the bucket
            (similarly to Numpy's `mean`).
            In both cases, empty buckets are set to NaN.
            Default: True

        Returns
        -------
        average : Dask array
            Binned and averaged data.
        """
        LOG.info("Get average value for each location")

        if not np.isnan(fill_value):
            data = da.where(data == fill_value, np.nan, data)

        sums = self.get_sum(data, skipna=skipna)
        counts = self.get_sum(np.logical_not(np.isnan(data)).astype(np.int64))

        average = sums / da.where(counts == 0, np.nan, counts)
        average = da.where(np.isnan(average), fill_value, average)

        return average

    def get_fractions(self, data, categories=None, fill_value=np.nan):
        """Get fraction of occurrences for each given categorical value.

        Parameters
        ----------
        data : Numpy or Dask array
            Categorical data to be processed
        categories : iterable or None
            One dimensional list of categories in the data, or None.  If None,
            categories are determined from the data by fully processing the
            data and finding the unique category values.
        fill_value : float
            Fill value to replace missing values.  Default: np.nan
        """

def _sort_weights(statistic_method, weights):
    """Sort idxs and weights based on weights.

    By default the method for sorting is `'min'`.
    """
    order = np.argsort(weights)
    if statistic_method == 'max':
        return order[::-1]
    return order

def _find_unique_bins_and_indices(bins, idxs_sorted):
    """Get unique bins and corresponding indices."""
    # get where the `idxs_sorted` located in `bins`
    binned_values = np.digitize(idxs_sorted, bins, right=True)

    # mask value outside of bin
    binned_values_masked = np.ma.masked_array(binned_values,
                                              (idxs_sorted < bins.min()) | (idxs_sorted > bins.max()))

    # get the first index and value in each bin
    return np.unique(binned_values_masked, return_index=True)

def _expand_bin_statistics(bins, unique_bin, unique_idx, weights_sorted):
    """Expand bin statistics to cover all bins."""
    # create the full index array
    weight_idx = np.full(len(bins), -1, dtype=np.int32)

    # assign the valid index to array
    weight_idx[unique_bin[~unique_bin.mask].data] = unique_idx[~unique_bin.mask]

    return weights_sorted[weight_idx]  # last value of weights_sorted always nan

def get_sample_from_neighbour_info(resample_type, output_shape, data,
                                   valid_input_index, valid_output_index,
                                   index_array, distance_array=None,
                                   weight_funcs=None, fill_value=0,
                                   with_uncert=False):
    """Resamples swath based on neighbour info.

    Parameters
    ----------
    resample_type : {'nn', 'custom'}
        'nn': Use nearest neighbour resampling
        'custom': Resample based on weight_funcs
    output_shape : (int, int)
        Shape of output as (rows, cols)
    data : numpy array
        Source data
    valid_input_index : numpy array
        valid_input_index from get_neighbour_info
    valid_output_index : numpy array
        valid_output_index from get_neighbour_info
    index_array : numpy array
        index_array from get_neighbour_info
    distance_array : numpy array, optional
        distance_array from get_neighbour_info
        Not needed for 'nn' resample type
    weight_funcs : list of function objects or function object, optional
        List of weight functions f(dist) to use for the weighting
        of each channel 1 to k.
        If only one channel is resampled weight_funcs is
        a single function object.
        Must be supplied when using 'custom' resample type
    fill_value : int, float, numpy floating, numpy integer or None, optional
        Set undetermined pixels to this value.
        If fill_value is None a masked array is returned
        with undetermined pixels masked

    Returns
    -------
    result : numpy array
        Source data resampled to target geometry
    """
    if data.ndim > 2 and data.shape[0] * data.shape[1] == valid_input_index.size:
        data = data.reshape(data.shape[0] * data.shape[1], data.shape[2])
    elif data.shape[0] != valid_input_index.size:
        data = data.ravel()

    if valid_input_index.size != data.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError('Mismatch between geometry and dataset')

    is_multi_channel = (data.ndim > 1)
    valid_input_size = valid_input_index.sum()
    valid_output_size = valid_output_index.sum()

    # Handle empty result set
    if valid_input_size == 0 or valid_output_size == 0:
        return _get_empty_sample(data, output_shape, is_multi_channel, fill_value)

    _validate_input_array(data, valid_input_index)
    _validate_resampler_type(resample_type, weight_funcs)

    if index_array.ndim == 1:
        neighbours = 1
    else:
        neighbours = index_array.shape[1]
        if resample_type == 'nn':
            raise ValueError('index_array contains more neighbours than '
                             'just the nearest')

    # Reduce data
    new_data = data[valid_input_index]

    # Nearest neighbour resampling should conserve data type
    input_data_type = new_data.dtype if resample_type == 'nn' else None

    # Handle masked array input
    is_masked_data = False
    if np.ma.is_masked(new_data):
        # Add the mask as channels to the dataset
        is_masked_data = True
        new_data = np.column_stack((new_data.data, new_data.mask))

    return _extract_resample_result(
        resample_type, neighbours, new_data, index_array, distance_array,
        valid_input_size, valid_output_index, weight_funcs, with_uncert,
        fill_value, output_shape, is_masked_data, is_multi_channel,
        input_data_type
    )

def unit(lon,lat):

    cth_xyz=np.stack(par.lonlat2xyz(lon,lat),axis=-1)*R
